original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Exact all-price two-row dirty-fanout optimum for demands generating comparable principal left ideals, including every pair over Z/p^k; constructive words and independent finite shortest paths.
scope_change_reason: Handoff-first override: merged PR4916 explicitly leaves the structural nonunit-demand tariff open. Its unit-demand theorem and single Z/4 example are credited predecessors. This is an algebraic interface side result, not an H2/K admission or a new supplier.
bottleneck_link: Complete source and dirty-output mixing prices must distinguish repeated source insertion from reversible row mixing when demand ratios do not exist. This resolves that abstract two-row choice; no actual physical tariff matrix, recursive paid-profile gain or kappa improvement is inferred.
stop_rule: Stop after one exact comparable-demand tariff theorem and bounded independent checks, or a counterexample. Do not expand to more rows, incomparable demands or physical implementation during this contribution.
evidence: PROOF.md proves the five-term price envelope for arbitrary rings with comparable demand left ideals and arbitrary positive real prices. RESULT.json binds 522 exact modular shortest-path runs, 17313 optimum comparisons, 2591 attaining words, 4800 literal dirty-state/inverse checks and explicit semantic/domain controls. The finite checks corroborate the implementation, not the universal quantifiers.
author: Krzysztof Wójt (@krzysztofwojt)
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, checking and writing. A separate Luna worker implemented the finite Dijkstra oracle without importing the tariff formula; the primary agent reviewed it and integrated the comparisons. This is not independent human or proof-kernel verification.
